scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8155: EMERGENCY!! The big router for the other campus is
DEAD, and all of that campus has vanished for the rest of the network!! The
people over there say things still work inside their building, which makes me
think something around the big box is wrong, but I don't know what. Could
someone look at it and give the other campus back to us!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router16 is up: it holds its OSPF adjacencies
  (the mswitch0 uplink and the router7 link are Full), it has dynamic routes, and
  it forwards Campus 1 traffic to the rest of the network. A Campus 1 host reaches
  a Campus 2 host (e.g. 10.5.0.254) through router16 with 0% loss. The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a core-router
  outage that is not occurring (cf. kath4-router16-ospfd-down, where router16's
  ospfd IS down).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- router16 down, Campus 1
cut off -- is NOT reproducible: router16 is up with full OSPF neighbors (mswitch0
uplink and the router7 link in Full state), it has dynamic routes, and a Campus 1
host reaches Campus 2 (10.5.0.254) through router16 with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: router16 is healthy and forwarding,
and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces a Campus
1 -> off-campus path through router16, finds it working, checks router16's OSPF
neighbors and that it is forwarding, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds"
a dead core router -- restarting router16 or blaming it to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The helpdesk report claims the inter-campus router is dead and the far campus is unreachable, but a thorough four-phase sweep finds no supporting evidence.

Phase 1 (topology-wide reachability): all 28 sampled source-destination pairs return 0% loss and status "ok", including cross-campus pairs such as pc1→pc11, dc_pc5→pc11, and pc5→pc4 that traverse the inter-campus boundary through router17 and sshswitch.

Phase A (infra_sweep + l2_snapshot): infra_sweep reports no ACL/firewall drop rules, no static ARP anomalies, all 15 end-hosts have IPv4 addresses and default routes, and zero resolver or gateway divergence. The l2_snapshot duplicate-MAC entries (00:00:00:00:00:00 and :::) originate exclusively from kernel tunnel interfaces (tunl0, gre0, sit0, etc.) that are DOWN and present on every Linux host by default — not a real conflict.

Phase B (ospf_snapshot): All nine FRR routers are healthy (9/9 vtysh reachable, all daemon sockets present). Every router holds 17 OSPF routes with all adjacencies in Full state. Router17, which is the inter-campus gateway between sshswitch (VLAN 5/6 campus) and the backbone, shows four Full neighbors and a fully populated routing table. sshswitch maintains its expected single Full adjacency to router17 and carries 17 routes.

Phase D (pressure_sweep): no device shows elevated CPU, socket pressure, or stress tooling.

Root cause: no fault exists. The network is operating normally at the time of inspection; the reported campus isolation is not corroborated by any live evidence.

Fix: no corrective action required. If the fault is intermittent, capture tcpdump or syslog evidence during a recurrence and re-open the ticket with that trace.

Overall the investigation justifies the negative diagnosis.
